Module 1

Work IQ — Copilot that knows your work

Work IQ is what turns Copilot from a smart chatbot into an assistant that knows your work. It grounds every answer in your emails, chats, meetings and files — only what you already have permission to see. In this module, you see where Work IQ sits in Copilot, how one request flows through it, what changes when you turn it on, and how Copilot can also act for you.

SourceMicrosoft IQ — Microsoft LearnModule 1 · 1 of 5Slide 3

1.3 Work IQ on/off — web-grounded vs. Work IQ–grounded chat

There aren't two separate chats anymore. There's one chat box with a single Work IQ toggle — flip it to control what Copilot grounds its answer in.

Work IQ off

Web-grounded Chat

Copilot answers from the web and the model’s training data, plus the files you hand it — none of your Microsoft 365 data. Prompt suggestions and the / references stay web- and file-based, so every prompt starts with you finding, attaching or pasting the material first.

  • Open-web knowledge
  • Plus any files you attach — and, in Outlook and Teams, the content you have open
  • Available to Basic & Premium
Work IQ on

Work IQ–grounded Chat

On by default. Copilot also reasons over your work across Microsoft 365 — emails, chats, meetings and files — trimmed to what you already have permission to see. The context is already there before you type.

  • Everything web-grounded does
  • Your emails, chats, meetings and files
  • Permission-trimmed — nothing you can't already open
Suggested prompts to try
Without Work IQ · English.pptx
Summarize the obligations under Indonesia’s Personal Data Protection Law (UU No. 27/2022) that apply to a bank’s customer-service and marketing teams, citing official sources. Deliver it as a 6-slide PowerPoint deck (.pptx) in blue and white: a title slide, one slide per obligation area and a final checklist slide.
Without Work IQ · Bahasa IndonesiaTabel
Cari siaran pers Bank Indonesia tentang keputusan BI-Rate dalam tiga bulan terakhir. Rangkum dalam tabel: tanggal, keputusan dan alasan utamanya. Lalu tulis tiga poin pembicaraan singkat untuk relationship manager saat berdiskusi dengan nasabah korporasi. Sertakan tautan sumber.
With Work IQ · English.html
Check my calendar for this week and my emails from the last three days. Create a one-page HTML briefing (.html) in BCA blue (#0066AE) and white: a day-by-day agenda with each meeting’s purpose and attendees, emails still waiting on my reply ranked by urgency, and the decisions I need to make.
With Work IQ · Bahasa Indonesia.xlsx
Rangkum email, chat Teams dan rapat saya dua minggu terakhir yang membahas perpanjangan fasilitas kredit nasabah korporasi. Untuk setiap nasabah, tampilkan apa yang sudah diputuskan, apa yang masih terbuka, penanggung jawab dan tenggat waktunya. Sajikan sebagai tabel, lalu buatkan file Excel (.xlsx) untuk dibagikan ke tim.

Notice the pattern. With Work IQ off, Copilot works from the public web — and any file you attach. That suits regulations, BI-Rate news and market facts, but it knows nothing about your own meetings, emails or chats.

The question moves to your actual work. You don’t paste or attach anything — Copilot finds the meetings, emails and chats itself, then delivers the result in the format you ask for.

It's one chat with a single Work IQ toggle — not two separate chat experiences.

Work IQ is part of Microsoft IQ — the intelligence platform that also brings Fabric IQ (Power BI and Fabric data), Foundry IQ and Web IQ. Work IQ is adding Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Power Platform data (public preview).

1.4 Work IQ in action — let Copilot act in your other apps

Copilot, grounded in Work IQ (part of Microsoft IQ), doesn't only read across your Microsoft 365 — it can also act. Ask Copilot Chat to draft an email, set up a meeting or post to Teams and it does the work, asking for your approval before it sends, posts, changes your calendar or shares content. Multi-step actions in Chat are rolling out through the Frontier program for users with a Microsoft Copilot license.

Draft an email — "Send the branch audit summary above to [regional operations head]" — Copilot drafts it and asks before sending.
Schedule a meeting — "Find 30 minutes with the credit review team next week and send the invite."
Reply in place — "Reply to the last email from Risk Management accepting the review and proposing Thursday."
Post to Teams — "Send these action items to our digital banking project channel."

Copilot drafts the email, meeting or post in the chat — you review it and approve before anything is sent, posted or scheduled. The action runs in Outlook, your calendar or Teams.

Module 2

Copilot Chat vs Cowork — and a Cowork deep dive

Copilot Chat and Cowork start from the same prompt box in Home. In Chat, Copilot answers and you act. In Cowork, you give Copilot an outcome — it plans the steps, acts across your apps and asks for your approval. In this module, you learn which one to use, and then you see how Cowork works.

Special tip — Design in Chat, deploy to Cowork

Make “design in Chat → deploy to Cowork” your default loop — the single biggest way to save Copilot Credits. For any important, ambiguous or repeated task, work across two surfaces:

Design in Chat

Plan the steps, draft and tighten the prompt, and preview the deliverable’s content and structure — all covered by your Premium license (USL) on Auto — no Copilot Credits.

→
Deploy in Cowork

Paste the finished prompt into a Cowork session to run the real multi-tool, multi-source execution — sending, scheduling and building files across your data.

Iterate in Chat (covered by your Premium license on Auto) until the prompt is right, then let Cowork do the work that consumes Copilot Credits once. Promote winning prompts into a custom skill or a recurring scheduled prompt so a single design keeps paying off.

Microsoft Copilot (Premium)
Cowork — deep dive

Cowork

The agent you hand an outcome rather than a question — it plans the steps, works across your apps for as long as the job takes, and checks with you before anything leaves the building.

Reaches for
Your Outlook, Teams, files and data — grounded in Work IQ, inside your own permissions
Trades
A single reply for a finished outcome — minutes to hours, running on its own
Gives you back
Real files in your OneDrive, a task you can reopen, and an approval gate before it sends

Cowork is the agentic side of Microsoft Copilot — you describe an outcome and it plans and carries out the steps for you, across your apps. You don’t build it: it’s a ready-made agentic system — open it from the prompt box in Home.

2.1 Copilot Chat vs Cowork — and a Cowork deep dive · continued
Custom skills — teach Copilot a task once

A skill is a modular capability you hand a session so it performs one specific task reliably and repeatably. It isn’t more knowledge and it isn’t another tool — it’s a packaged procedure, with the assets and scripts that procedure needs travelling alongside it. The one-line distinction worth remembering: an agent is the “who”; a skill is the “how”. Add a skill when a task must be done the same way every single time — your report format, your naming convention, your review checklist.

1Create it
From the Customize pageOpen Customize in Cowork and describe the task — e.g. a document format you produce every week.
By asking in chatDescribe the procedure in plain language, ask Cowork to save it as a skill, then review it.
By hand, or uploadWrite a SKILL.md — or select Upload skill for a .md, .zip or .skill file.
2The skill package — the “how”
OneDrive › Documents › Cowork › skills
SKILL.mdName and description (when to use it) + the step-by-step procedure · up to 1 MB
Companion filesTemplates, checklists, reference data, scripts · up to 20 files, 10 MB per skill
Up to 50 custom skills
3Cowork uses it
Discovered at session startA skill added mid-session loads in the next one.
Applied when the task matchesThe same procedure, every time — your format, naming or checklist.
Checked for qualityA plain-language quality report when you create, update or validate it.

Where they live, and when they load. Custom skills are stored as SKILL.md files in your OneDrive at /Documents/Cowork/skills/ — up to 50 of them. Cowork discovers your skills at the start of each session, so a skill you add mid-session isn’t picked up until the next one. The same applies to plugins: removing one takes effect in the next session, never mid-flight. Skill scripts run in a temporary, isolated environment inside the Microsoft 365 service boundary, removed when the task finishes . When you create, update or validate a skill, Cowork returns a plain-language quality report — still review a new skill’s output like a colleague’s first draft. Each SKILL.md can be up to 1 MB, with up to 20 companion files (10 MB per skill); custom skills aren’t supported in Cowork on mobile. Skills you create in Copilot Chat also work in Cowork; Cowork skills appear in Chat when you share them.

Module 3

Creating Dashboards with Microsoft Copilot

Copilot can turn your data — for example, a branch performance workbook in Excel — into a dashboard. Where you keep the dashboard changes how it works. In this module, you learn what a dashboard is. Then you learn why an .html file and an .aspx page work differently in OneDrive and SharePoint.

SourceIntroduction to dashboards for Power BI designers — Microsoft LearnModule 3 · 1 of 6Slide 13
3.1 Anatomy of a Dashboard

A dashboard is one screen that shows your most important metrics. You use it to monitor your work at a glance. When the data changes, the dashboard shows the new data.

Dashboard = Data + Visuals

Power BI gives a good reference definition: “A Power BI dashboard is a single page, often called a canvas, that tells a story through visualizations.” Every dashboard has the same five layers. The data goes up from layer 1 to layer 5:

5

Delivery surface

Where people see the dashboard: the Power BI service, a SharePoint page, an HTML file, or a screen in an app

4

Visuals

KPI cards, charts, tables and filters. On a Power BI dashboard, these are tiles

3

Model & calculations

Tables, relationships, measures and KPIs. In Power BI, this is a semantic model

2

Connection & refresh

How the data comes in and how current it is: a live link, a scheduled refresh, an API call, or a one-time snapshot

1

Data sources

Excel workbooks in OneDrive or SharePoint, SharePoint lists, Dataverse, databases, on-premises systems

Identity & permissions

Applies to all layers: who can open the dashboard, and which data each viewer can see

SourceIntroduction to dashboards for Power BI designers — Microsoft LearnModule 3 · 2 of 6Slide 14
3.2 Comparison Table: .html vs .aspx in OneDrive/SharePoint

You may have prompted Copilot to turn [/Branch Performance FY26.xlsx] into an interactive .html dashboard. In this section, the data is in one Excel file that is stored on your SharePoint site. Copilot makes one .html file, and the dashboard works in the Copilot preview. What happens next depends on where you put the file. There are three formats:

  • .html as an artifact in OneDrive/SharePoint — a file in a library. SharePoint and OneDrive do not run its script. The dashboard shows only a snapshot of the Excel file.
  • .html as a custom SharePoint page — you upload the file to the Site Pages library, and SharePoint shows it as an HTML page of the site. This feature is rolling out through the Frontier program.
  • .aspx as a site page — a modern SharePoint page in Site Pages that you build from web parts.
Aspect.html as an artifact in OneDrive/SharePoint.html as a custom SharePoint page.aspx as a site page
What it isA standalone web file: markup, styles and script in one file.Your .html file, published as an HTML page of the site. The page stays in Site Pages; its images and other assets go to Site Assets.A modern SharePoint page (an ASP.NET page) that you build from web parts.
How you publish itSave or upload the file to OneDrive or a document library.Site Pages › Create or upload › Upload HTML page (or Upload HTML folder).
Or, in a document library: … › Edit › Edit in SharePoint. This moves the file to Site Pages.		Site Pages › Create or upload › Site Page. Then add web parts.
Where the logic runsNowhere. SharePoint and OneDrive do not run its script: they download the file or show its raw content.In a sandboxed iframe inside the site header, navigation and footer, with Content Security Policy (CSP) rules. JavaScript in the same file runs.In the web parts. They run in the browser, as the signed-in viewer.
Viewer sign-inThe OneDrive/SharePoint rules. Library permissions decide who can open or download the file.The SharePoint rules. Page permissions decide who can view the page.The SharePoint rules. Site and page permissions decide who can view the page.

Best forA snapshot that people open or download from the library.Your own design, from an existing .html file, with live data from the Excel file.A standard team page that shows the Excel file, or custom code with SPFx.

Rule of thumb. An .html artifact in a library shows only a snapshot of the Excel file. For live data from the Excel file, publish the .html to Site Pages as an HTML page, or build an .aspx site page with web parts.

Module 4

Creating Apps with Microsoft Copilot Code

An app lets people enter data and act on it — a dashboard only reads and shows data. With Code in the Microsoft Copilot app, you describe the app in plain language and Copilot builds it. In this module, you learn what Code is and the difference between a static and an interactive app. Then you watch Code build and publish an app, and you learn how to build one step by step.

SourceCopilot Code overview — Microsoft LearnModule 4 · 1 of 6Slide 19
Microsoft Copilot (Premium)Preview · Frontier
4.1 Code

Code is a separate tab in the Microsoft Copilot app, next to Chat and Cowork. The Code tab turns what you describe into working software. You describe the result in natural language. Code builds it and shows it on a canvas next to the conversation.

  • What it makes — apps, dashboards, internal tools, static websites, data transforms, automations and scripts.
  • Where it runs — on your device, in a project folder that you select, or in a secure, isolated environment in the cloud. On your device, Code asks for your approval before it goes outside that folder, makes a network connection or runs a terminal command.
  • Technology — Code uses the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot. It runs in a sandboxed environment.
  • Publish — a static app is shared as a link for your organization. An interactive app is published to Copilot Managed Runtime (see 4.2).
  • Control — admins can audit the actions of Copilot Code: the code that it generated, the commands that it ran, and the files that it read or wrote.

License and status. The Microsoft Copilot license controls access to Copilot Code. Usage counts against your Microsoft Copilot entitlement, and admins can set a spend limit for each user. Copilot Code is in the Frontier preview program. Deep dive: to build an app with Code, step by step, go to 4.4.

4.2 Static and Interactive App

Copilot Code makes two kinds of app. A static app is a set of files that runs in the browser of the viewer. An interactive app is published to Copilot Managed Runtime. It signs users in and connects to organizational data.

Built in the Code tab, in the cloud

4.4 Build Your App with Code

This is the deep dive for 4.1. You need an active Microsoft Copilot license and access to the Frontier preview program. Code works in the Microsoft Copilot desktop app and on the web (cloud only). Do these steps:

  1. Open the Microsoft Copilot app, or go to copilot.cloud.microsoft. Select Code in the tab switcher at the top.
  2. Select Create new to start a project.
  3. Describe the app. To add context, select + to upload files or attach your work context.
  4. Select where the project runs: on your device (local) or in the cloud. Select a model, or keep Auto (cloud only). Select a mode: Interactive (the default), Plan or Automatic.
  5. Look at the canvas next to the conversation. It shows the app while Code builds it.
  6. To change the app, describe the change or select an element on the canvas. To undo a change, ask Code to revert to an earlier version. Code saves the project automatically.
  7. To share a static app, share it as a link for your organization (cloud only). For the difference between a static app and an interactive app, see 4.2.
  8. To make an interactive app live, write “Publish it” or “Make it live”. Code publishes the app to Copilot Managed Runtime. Users open it at managedapps.cloud.microsoft.
  9. Share the published app with a link, as you share a document. Sharing an app does not share its data.

Module 5

Creating Agentic Workflows with Copilot Studio

An agent decides its next step itself. Sometimes you must have the same steps each time — for example, a credit limit approval or a weekly complaint summary. For this work, Copilot Studio has flows: agent flows and workflows. In this module, you learn what an agentic workflow is. Then you compare the two types of flow and build one of each.

SourceAgent flows overview — Microsoft LearnModule 5 · 1 of 8Slide 25
5.1 Anatomy of an Agentic Workflow

An agentic workflow is an automation that has a fixed path with AI steps on it. The maker designs the path before it runs. AI actions and agents do some of the steps. Microsoft describes workflows as automations that “combine deterministic automation with AI-driven actions, such as agent handoffs and native AI nodes.”

Agent = LLM + Harness

The model plans the steps, selects tools and decides when the work is done. The harness is “the operating layer between the model and the agent’s configuration”. Your instructions, tools and knowledge go through it.

Flow = Trigger + Actions

The maker designs the path before it runs. The path has rule-based branches. The harness under the flow decides the designer, the AI steps and the billing.

Trigger

On demand, on a schedule, on an event, or when an agent calls it

→

Connector

Microsoft 365, third-party or custom

→

AI capability

Generate text, process documents, run a prompt, call an agent

→

Human in the loop

Request information or approval

→

Built-in tools

Branches, loops, data operations, child flows

Same anatomy, two harnesses. An agent flow is Trigger + Actions on the standard harness. A workflow is Trigger + Actions on the GitHub Copilot harness, with native Agent, Copilot and Classify nodes.

SourceAgent flows overview — Microsoft Learn · Workflows overview (GitHub Copilot) — Microsoft Learn · FAQ for workflows (GitHub Copilot) — Microsoft Learn · Harnesses in Copilot Studio — Microsoft LearnModule 5 · 2 of 8Slide 26

Copilot Studio has two types of flow. They have the same anatomy (Trigger + Actions) on a different harness.

AspectAgent Flows (Standard Harness)Workflow (GHCP Harness)
What it isAn automation on the standard harness, managed with classic agents.An automation on the GitHub Copilot harness.

Path — key differenceDeterministic: the same input always gives the same output.Predictable, but results can change when actions use AI or changing data.

How to select. Use an agent flow when every step is fixed and the same input must give the same output. Use a workflow when the path is fixed but some steps need AI judgment, for example to classify an item or to call Copilot or an agent. You cannot convert an agent flow into a workflow.

5.3 Build your Agent Flow (Standard Harness)

An agent flow gives the same output for the same input. Use it for fixed, repeated procedures. Agent flows are on the standard harness, so you start from Other ways to build.

Do these steps:

1

Go to copilotstudio.microsoft.com. On the Home page, select Other ways to build.

2

Under Build with standard orchestration, select Agent flows (Standard). Other path: Workflows › the arrow next to New workflow › Agent flows.

Billing. Each action consumes Copilot Credits from Copilot Studio capacity. When an agent calls the flow for a signed-in user with a Microsoft Copilot license, the flow run does not consume Copilot Studio capacity. This does not apply to autonomous runs.

2

5.4 Build your Workflow (GHCP Harness)

A workflow mixes fixed steps with native AI nodes. Use it when the path is fixed but some steps need judgment. Workflows are on the GitHub Copilot harness, so you start from the Workflow tile on the Home page.

Every Monday at 8 AM, read the new customer complaints. Classify each complaint as card, digital banking or account. Send digital banking complaints to the support agent. Ask Copilot to write a weekly summary and post it in the team channel.

Billing. Workflows consume Copilot Credits from Copilot Studio capacity, from the first build step, including preview and testing. They do not need a separate Power Automate license.

5.4 Build your Workflow (GHCP Harness) · continued

Do these steps:

1

Go to copilotstudio.microsoft.com. On the Home page, select the Workflow tile (GitHub Copilot). Other path: Workflows › New workflow.

2

Change Untitled workflow to a name.

3

Select the Start node to set the trigger: on demand, on a schedule or on an event. To let an agent call the workflow, use the When an agent calls the flow trigger and a Respond to the agent action.

4

Add steps from the Add pane, or select + next to a node: Agent, Classify, Extract, Copilot, Human review, Connector, Function, Variable, If/Else, Loop and Note.

5

Test one node with Test this node, or select Test (▷) to run the full workflow. Correct all errors. Select Review, then Publish. You cannot publish a workflow that has errors.
